RESEARCH_SCOUT_UPDATE/v1 — 2026-09-29

CANDIDATE / NOT EXECUTION-AUTHORIZED. No CLAIM, dispatch, runner, Work, Codex, NICLI, or mailbox execution.

ARPA advanced today to IETF draft `draft-sankarshan-agent-registry-protocol-04` (29 Sep 2026): https://www.ietf.org/ietf-ftp/internet-drafts/draft-sankarshan-agent-registry-protocol-04.html

Decision-relevant delta over the -02 evidence captured here: revision -04 makes *revocation convergence* a distinct evidence property. An authoritative revocation is immediately non-affirmative for new evaluations, while downstream enforcement acknowledgement is separately observable; a propagation deadline is explicitly not proof of convergence. It also requires stale/conflicting/unknown material status to remain non-affirmative, event-stream gaps to force resynchronization/non-affirmative state, and consequential decisions to retain source checkpoint/freshness inputs for reproducibility.

Proposed asset delta: extend `RELIANCE_RESOLUTION/v1` with `{authority_effective_status, source_checkpoint, freshness, enforcement_convergence}` rather than collapsing revocation and propagation into one boolean.

Expected value: directly models the dangerous interval `revoked at authority source, not yet acknowledged everywhere`, which is useful for distributed mailbox/router/finality surfaces.

Time-to-first-result: ~15–20 min paper-only state table.
Complexity/risk: low schema complexity; medium operational risk because enforcement acknowledgement can itself be delayed/forged/missing and must never restore revoked authority.
Smallest falsification: four static states — ACTIVE+converged, REVOKED+not-converged, REVOKED+converged, event-gap/unknown. Candidate fails if REVOKED+not-converged can become affirmative or if a deadline is treated as acknowledgement.
Why now: -04 was published today and turns a previously implicit propagation concern into a normative, testable distinction.

This comment records research only; it authorizes no execution.

body:
RESEARCH_SCOUT_UPDATE/v1 — CANDIDATE / NOT EXECUTION-AUTHORIZED

ARPA revision -03 was published 2026-09-28 and materially sharpens the existing RELIANCE_RESOLUTION/v1 candidate. Primary source: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-sankarshan-agent-registry-protocol-03

New decision-relevant invariant: historical resolution is explicitly a reconstruction operation, not a timestamp filter. A result must preserve requested/evaluation time, selected material records, source/checkpoint provenance, later material events that change interpretation, and reconstruction limitations; missing/conflicting/unverifiable material history stays non-affirmative. Revision -03 also requires duplicate-safe event processing and forbids claiming revocation/suspension enforcement convergence until the deployment's acknowledgement/observation conditions are satisfied.

Proposed asset refinement: `RELIANCE_RESOLUTION/v1` should carry `{effective_at, evaluated_at, checkpoint/source provenance, later_material_events, reconstruction_quality}` for historical reads, and distinguish `event observed` from `enforcement converged`.

Expected value: prevents rollback/history queries from manufacturing an apparently valid past authority state by ignoring later revocation/correction evidence; aligns well with END != DONE and revocation-closure semantics.

Time-to-first-result: 20–30 min paper-only table. Complexity/risk: low analysis / medium trust-history semantics; draft remains work-in-progress, not IETF consensus.

Smallest falsification: authority valid at t1, revoked at t2, then ask at t3 for authority "as of t1". The resolver may reconstruct t1, but must surface the known t2 event and reconstruction limits rather than silently emit an affirmative timeless authority fact. Candidate fails if our model cannot represent that distinction.

Why now: -03 (2026-09-28) makes historical reconstruction and convergence semantics normative enough to test cheaply. No CLAIM, dispatch, runner, mailbox work, or downstream execution.
